flagSemantics.verdict: CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_ENABLED is a hardcoded false CONSTANT in source (JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:83), not a runtime-read env var. It gates exactly two things: (1) createDefaultCampaignEventStore's choice between JournalCampaignEventStore and InMemoryCampaignEventStore for co-op match/host creation (JournalCampaignEventStore.ts:463), and (2) via isCampaignJournalAuthorityEnabled() (which ORs it with a second, narrower e2e-only arm), whether campaign CREATE ([id].ts:249) or ADOPT (adopt.ts:145) writes a real genesis event + journal-native marker to the real SQLite database.
flagSemantics.e2eArm: MEKSTATION_E2E_CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY is a genuine env var, but campaignJournalAuthorityEnabled.ts:23-28 requires it to be exactly '1' AND requires process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE === 'true' in the SAME process before e2eJournalAuthorityArmed() returns true. NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE is set only by playwright.config.ts's webServer.env (never in a real deployment), so this arm is structurally unreachable in production by design (the module's own header comment: 'Both keys are required so a production process can never arm this'). Its ONLY existing production caller (adopt.ts:145, [id].ts:249, matches/index.ts:267) makes it a genesis/adoption-time write gate, not a per-request authority check.
flagSemantics.criticalDistinction: POST /api/campaigns/[id]/commands (commands.ts:130-145) does NOT read CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_ENABLED or isCampaignJournalAuthorityEnabled() at all. It calls resolveCampaignAuthorityFromStores, which reads ONLY the persisted campaign_authority_migration marker row (resolveCampaignAuthorityFromStores.ts:44-58) and, if that marker's state is 'journal', probes the real SQLite journal for a stream. executeCampaignCommand (campaignCommandPipeline.ts:317-320) then gates purely on deps.authority.kind === 'journal'. This means: once a campaign's DURABLE MARKER says 'journal' -- by ANY means, flag or no flag -- POST /commands routes real commands to the real SQLite-backed journal identically in production and in a spawned e2e process. The flag only controls how a campaign FIRST reaches the 'journal' marker state at creation/adoption time; it does not gate command execution at all.
flagSemantics.answerToQ1: Spinning up a standalone server process with MEKSTATION_E2E_CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY=1 (and NEXT_PUBLIC_E2E_MODE=true) set, so that campaign CREATE writes a real journal marker via the e2e arm, IS 'an E2E-only flag used as production proof' in the sense the acceptance line forbids: that specific code branch (isCampaignJournalAuthorityEnabled() returning true through the e2e OR) can never execute in a real deployment, so a proof built on it demonstrates a path production cannot take. The legitimate alternative -- reachable without any flag -- is to construct the marker directly via writeCampaignMigrationMarker(createJournalNativeMarker(campaignId)) against the real SQLite file (the same technique src/__tests__/api/campaigns/campaignAuthorityBlocked.test.ts already uses at :85,:106,:130, just against a real file path instead of :memory:). Once written this way, POST /commands on either process routes to the real journal through the SAME code path (resolveCampaignAuthorityFromStores + executeCampaignCommand) a genuinely-cutover production campaign would use -- because that path never distinguishes how the marker got there. The CO3 receipt MUST state explicitly: 'the campaign's journal-authority marker was constructed by calling writeCampaignMigrationMarker directly against the spawned server's real SQLite file; MEKSTATION_E2E_CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY and CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_ENABLED were both left at their production values (unset / false) throughout the run' -- and should assert this negatively (grep the child processes' env, or assert the response body's journalAuthorityEnabled field stayed false where surfaced e.g. matches/index.ts:267) so the receipt is falsifiable rather than merely asserted.

seatTopology.correctionToParentBrief: The CO3 slice description in the parent admission brief (roadmap.json:6306-... referencing r2-authority-cutover-admission-brief-20260915.json slices[3].nonClaims) states CO3 'uses a co-op-seated campaign, same as the existing two-device spec's fixtures'. Read directly, this is IMPRECISE: e2e/campaign-two-device-drive.spec.ts creates its campaign via a plain PUT /api/campaigns/[id] with baseVersion 0 (spec.ts:302) and its own header explicitly states the share step is deliberately WITHOUT a bearer token because 'this campaign has no co-op session and therefore no participants' (spec.ts:14-19). That spec never creates a campaign_session_participant row and could not pass isActiveCampaignSeat for any player. It is not a valid template for the seat half of CO3.
seatTopology.validTopology: A co-op HOST match creation is the one existing path that binds an active seat: POST /api/multiplayer/matches with a coopCampaign payload triggers commitCoopCampaignAuthority (matches/index.ts:243-262), which calls commitCampaignCreationCheckpoint with gmParticipantId: hostPlayerId, binding the host as the durable GM participant (campaignCreationCheckpoint.ts header, migration-17 membership) BEFORE the match-creation response is acknowledged. e2e/helpers/gmTwoPlayerAuthorityRecovery.ts:202 already drives this exact call from a Playwright test (used by e2e/gm-two-player-authority-recovery.pack.spec.ts) and is the directly reusable harness for CO3's seat step -- not campaign-two-device-drive.spec.ts.
seatTopology.tokenPath: Once the host is bound as an active participant, a bearer token scoped to that campaign is minted the same way campaign-two-device-drive.spec.ts's 'dial' step already does (spec.ts imports issuePlayerToken from @/lib/multiplayer/client/issuePlayerToken and encodeTokenForWire from @/types/multiplayer/Player) -- that machinery is orthogonal to campaign vs. multiplayer-match participants and is reusable verbatim for the host's own token.
seatTopology.answerToQ2: The topology that reaches /commands today is a co-op session with a HOST participant (GM) bound via the match-creation checkpoint -- not a plain single-player campaign, and not campaign-two-device-drive.spec.ts's grant/replica topology (which has no participants at all). CO3 needs to create its journal-authority campaign as (or promote it into) a co-op-hosted campaign via POST /api/multiplayer/matches, mint a token for the bound host player id, then use that token for POST /commands on the source process. This does not touch the single-player seat gap at all -- consistent with the owner decision staying open and out of scope for CO3.

sequencing: 1. Spawn process A (source) via startSecondServer's pattern, or reuse Playwright's own webServer as process A -- pointed at a fresh temp DATABASE_PATH.

2. Through process A: POST /api/multiplayer/matches with coopCampaign to create a co-op-hosted campaign; this binds the host as an active campaign_session_participant AND (per matches/index.ts:257-267) runs commitCoopCampaignAuthority, which itself passes journalAuthorityEnabled: isCampaignJournalAuthorityEnabled() -- expected FALSE in this run, so the checkpoint's genesis-branch step is a no-op and the campaign is created on ORDINARY (non-journal) authority at this point. This is intentional: CO3 is proving the CUTOVER machinery, not relying on it to fire automatically.

3. From the TEST process (not process A or B), open a SEPARATE SQLiteService instance pointed at the SAME DATABASE_PATH process A is using, and call writeCampaignMigrationMarker(createJournalNativeMarker(campaignId)) to move the campaign onto journal authority WITHOUT touching any flag. This must happen while process A is not mid-write to avoid a WAL lock collision -- sequencing detail flagged under openQuestions.
4. Mint a bearer token for the bound host player id (issuePlayerToken), scoped to the campaign.
5. Spawn process B pointed at the SAME DATABASE_PATH as process A (the deliberate deviation from campaign-two-device-drive.spec.ts's separate-file replica case).
6. POST /api/campaigns/[campaignId]/commands on process A with the host token and a real intent; assert 200 and inspect the response/journal head.

7. GET /api/campaigns/[campaignId] (or a lower-level journal read) on process B; assert the committed event/derived state is visible -- same-file convergence, no in-memory sharing between the two Node processes.

8. Kill process A (or B) mid-scenario using scripts/e2e/relaunching-server.mjs's spawn/respawn shape; re-spawn pointed at the SAME DATABASE_PATH; assert (a) the marker and journal history survive the OS-level restart (restart-never-creates-fresh-log, per task 5.7's own acceptance text) and (b) a fresh command/read after respawn still converges.

9. Optionally, a rollback-refused row: after step 6's committed command, attempt scripts/campaign-authority-cutover.ts's rollback verb (once #1739/#1740 land) against the same campaign and assert it is prohibited (CO2's D10 guard) -- the parent brief explicitly recommends deferring this to AFTER the base convergence proof lands, in a separate slice ordering, so CO2's own wiring gap risk doesn't block CO3's baseline proof.
assertions: Process A's POST /commands response is 200 with the expected result shape (not 'blocked'/403).

Process B's GET reflects the committed event/derived field WITHOUT any in-memory sharing -- i.e., process B was started fresh, never held a live connection to process A's application state, only to the shared SQLite file.
After killing and respawning one process, a repeat read/write cycle still converges (restart-never-creates-fresh-log).

Negative/falsifiability assertion: MEKSTATION_E2E_CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY and CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_ENABLED were never set to an armed value in EITHER spawned process's env for the duration of the run (assert on the env objects passed to spawn(), not just absence of a crash).
nonClaims: Does not flip CAMPAIGN_JOURNAL_AUTHORITY_ENABLED in production; the constant stays false, verified structurally (no source file touched under src/lib/campaign/sync/) and behaviorally (the negative assertion above).
Does not address the single-player identity/seat owner decision -- the proof deliberately uses a co-op-hosted campaign, which is a real, already-implemented topology, not a workaround.

Does not re-prove replica/grant sync across SEPARATE database files -- that is what e2e/campaign-two-device-drive.spec.ts already proves (per PR #1341 lineage); CO3 proves SAME-file multi-process convergence for the authority/journal machinery specifically, which is a distinct property.

CO3 can reuse this exact constant/env var for process B, so on this machine (port 3639 per the task brief's framing) CO3 would run with MEKSTATION_E2E_PORT=3639 (or whatever the primary lane uses) for process A/Playwright's own webServer, and either the existing MEKSTATION_E2E_SECOND_PORT default (3617) or an explicit override for process B -- no collision with 3639, no new port-derivation code needed.
runnability.localExecutability: The spec pattern (spawn a second `node server.js`, poll a readiness URL, drain stdio) already runs successfully in this repo's e2e lane per campaign-two-device-drive.spec.ts's own existence and the umbrella-21.x restart harness (relaunching-server.mjs) already used by E2E-05/06/15. Nothing in that pattern is CI-only or requires infrastructure this machine lacks. The genuinely NEW risk is step 3 above (a third SQLiteService instance, from the TEST process itself, writing directly to a file two OTHER live Node processes also hold open in WAL mode) -- SQLiteService.ts:83 sets `journal_mode = WAL`, which is designed for multi-reader/single-writer concurrent access and should tolerate this, but no test in this codebase currently exercises three separate better-sqlite3 Database handles against one file concurrently on Windows; this is EXPECTED to work (WAL is designed for exactly this) but is UNVERIFIED by any existing test and should be the first thing CO3's author confirms with a throwaway probe before writing the full spec.
runnability.answerToQ4: Yes, CO3 is runnable on this machine with only the primary e2e port (3639 or whatever is assigned) plus the already-existing MEKSTATION_E2E_SECOND_PORT mechanism for the second process -- no new port-derivation logic is needed.
